Devin Laurent

life-010 · holdout · fictional age 16

Written life first, then interpreted by a separate response author without the engine or results. These are synthetic checks. There is no correct career answer key.

Life from age 4 to 16

I enjoy making a gathering happen, and I might still leave early once it is happening. I do not have one big plan; I want to try something long enough to know whether I like the everyday parts.

  • family: Lives with his mother and stepmother; an adult half-sister visits frequently.
  • finances: Low-to-moderate income with dependable rent and essentials.
  • geography: Apartment complex in Baton Rouge, Louisiana; relatives in Beaumont, Texas.
  • cultureLanguages: English; family preserves some Louisiana Creole recipes and expressions.
  • school: Public high school with a strong culinary elective and limited advanced sciences.
  • accessOpportunities: Community center and relatives can support occasional Texas campus trips.
  • Age 4–5

    In 2014, Devin spent time in his grandmother’s kitchen and disliked sticky dough on his hands. He preferred arranging the serving table, counting chairs, and deciding where everyone could sit without blocking the doorway.

  • Age 6–7

    At six, he joined a recreation-center chess group. In 2017, he lost many games to an older neighbor but returned because reviewing the game afterward felt like solving a puzzle with another person.

  • Age 8–9

    In 2018, Devin began weekend visits to cousins in Beaumont. Their crowded, cheerful house made him curious about different routines, and he started keeping a notebook comparing bus routes and public playgrounds between the cities.

  • Age 10–11

    During 2020, he shared a laptop with his mother and learned to plan work around her evening classes. He cooked simple meals despite still disliking some textures, using utensils and gloves when they helped.

  • Age 12–13

    At twelve, Devin tried basketball and decided he preferred keeping score to playing. By 2023, he was helping a community-center coach settle scheduling disagreements and discovering that adults sometimes needed the same reminders as children.

  • Age 14–15

    In 2024, a culinary elective made him interested in safe food storage and scaling recipes. In 2025, he volunteered for event setup, enjoying the planning while sometimes finding the constant conversation afterward unexpectedly tiring.

  • Age 16

    At sixteen in 2026, Devin is comparing Louisiana options with Texas programs near family in Beaumont. He likes the idea of college but is equally interested in whether a short credential would give him something tangible to build on.

Life now

  • enjoys: Chess analysis · Planning table layouts · Testing recipe proportions
  • avoids: Sticky textures · Noisy celebrations after long workdays
  • activities: Community-center scheduling · Culinary elective · Weekend cooking
  • demonstratedSkills: Scales quantities · Tracks schedules · Explains game mistakes patiently
  • unfamiliarActivities: Campus housing · Advanced laboratory work
  • motivations: Predictable teamwork · Seeing a plan function
  • ambitions: Explore study near extended family · Earn a useful first qualification · He imagines a dependable home near relatives, a few close friendships, and a daily rhythm with both busy collaboration and quiet hours.
  • struggles: Understates his own preferences · Needs quiet recovery after events
  • supports: Mothers · Half-sister · Community coach
  • practicalConstraints: Travel budget · Shared computer · School course limitations

Still uncertain: Would event planning remain enjoyable under deadline pressure? · Is Texas appealing because of programs or because cousins are there?
